metaDescription: Family land near Orange Beach, AL sold for resort development but you kept the minerals? Get a title-checked offer, no pressure to sign.
heroLead: Orange Beach went from fishing camps and family homesteads to one of the busiest resort corridors on the Gulf Coast in the span of a couple of generations, and the mineral rights under some of that land never made the trip along with the condos.
intro: When coastal Baldwin County land got sold for resort and residential development starting in the later twentieth century, developers were buying surface rights for construction, not thinking much about what might sit deeper below — the same pattern that's played out across a lot of coastal Alabama. Families that once fished and farmed near Orange Beach sometimes kept the mineral estate even as the surface transformed entirely, and those interests can sit forgotten for decades while the land above them turns into an entirely different economy.

sections.heading: What a Beach Boom Sale Actually Conveyed
paragraphs: If your family sold land near Orange Beach during the resort development years, the deed language determines whether minerals went with it or stayed with your family. We read that language directly rather than assuming a beachfront sale automatically included everything below the surface.

sections.heading: Deep Gulf Coast Gas Tests Onshore Baldwin County
paragraphs: Baldwin County has seen exploratory interest in the deep Norphlet and Smackover trend that runs through south Alabama and into the Gulf, and coastal acreage near Orange Beach has occasionally drawn leasing activity tied to that deeper play, separate from the shallower production more common further inland. We check whether your specific tract has ever been part of that leasing history.

faqs.question: Our family sold beachfront land to a developer decades ago. Could we still own the minerals?
faqs.answer: It's possible, depending on the deed language. We read the specific reservation before telling you either way.

faqs.question: Is there any real oil and gas activity this close to the coast?
faqs.answer: Some exploratory leasing tied to the deep Norphlet-Smackover trend has occurred in coastal Baldwin County. We check your tract's specific history rather than assuming based on the resort development around it.

faqs.question: Does resort development on the surface affect what a mineral interest is worth?
faqs.answer: Not directly — mineral value depends on leasing and production history, not what's built above ground. We evaluate it on its own terms.

faqs.question: Our family holds a small fractional interest from an old homestead. Is it worth pursuing given how built up the area is now?
faqs.answer: Yes, it's worth confirming. We research the actual leasing history for your fraction regardless of how the surface has changed since.
